summary: The change replaces unguarded DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0] indexing with FirstOrDefault() for the MemberNeedsKey and BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull diagnostic locations in TypeCollector.cs, which is the root cause: closed generic value types from referenced assemblies have symbols with no syntax (including compiler-generated backing fields), so the old [0] access threw IndexOutOfRangeException and crashed the source generator (missing generated resolver). The new regression test fails on base and passes on head, the full suite has no regressions, and the only blemish is a new SA1515 style warning in the test file.

requirement_verdicts.confidence_basis: The new regression test passes on head and fails on base because MyGenericStructFormatter`1.g.cs is missing (the generator crashed), and TypeCollector.cs head line 1077 now uses FirstOrDefault() for the MemberNeedsKey location instead of indexing DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0], which was the crash site for syntax-less metadata members.

facts.json records no analyzer execution or AD0001 check for this input; the executed test is a source-generator verification whose base failure was a missing generated file (CS8785), not an analyzer exception. The code fix removes the IndexOutOfRangeException in the shared TypeCollector diagnostic path, but no analyzer run confirms the analyzer does not throw on this input.

For members with no syntax (metadata/referenced-assembly types), the diagnostic location is now FirstOrDefault()?.GetSyntax().GetLocation(), which yields null rather than a location outside the compilation, and non-public metadata members such as backing fields are not reported unless non-public members are serialized; the test passes without the generator emitting fatal diagnostics.

findings.claim: The new test marks the property with [Key(0)], so intKey is non-null and the intKey == null && stringKey == null branch at line 985 is never reached; mutation M1 (remove_call on that line) survived with no test killing it. findings.suggested_fix: Add a regression case where a metadata-declared value type member has no usable key (both int and string key null) so the BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull path is covered by a test that fails without the FirstOrDefault() guard.

The build still passes, but the analyzer warning count increases.
